articles.title: Anthropic to debut on Wall Street with a $1.5 trillion valuation in the biggest IPO of all time
articles.summary: OAKLAND, Calif. (AP) — Anthropic priced its initial public offering at $83 per share Wednesday, valuing the artificial intelligence giant at $1.5 trillion in the biggest Wall Street debut of all time.

articles.title: Chinese national wanted for assault, making death threats outside Chinese Consulate
articles.summary: Toronto police say a 41-year-old Chinese national is wanted following an assault at a demonstration outside the Chinese Consulate in September. Investigators say just after 9:30 a.m. on September 22, a man approached some demonstrators outside the consulate on St. George Street just south of Bernard Avenue, allegedly causing damage to their signs and banners. articles.title: Skydance to combine Warner Bros. TV Group and Paramount Television Studios
articles.summary: NEW YORK (AP) — Skydance will combine two of its key TV production units, Warner Bros. Television Group and Paramount Television Studios, bringing such shows as "The Pitt,” “Ted Lasso,” “Reacher” and “Landman” under the same roof.

articles.title: Rob Manfred says MLB owners won’t compromise on a salary cap, leaving sport headed to a lockout
articles.summary: NEW YORK (AP) — Major League Baseball Commissioner Rob Manfred said owners will not move off their demand for a salary cap, leaving the sport on track for a lockout starting Dec. 2 that could threaten the 2027 season.

articles.title: Inquest into police-involved death of Jamal Francique shown videos from after shooting
articles.summary: The inquest into the death of a Black man shot by police in Mississauga in early 2020 is watching videos showing the officers around his wrecked car after the shooting.

articles.title: From frontlines to city hall: Newly elected advocates determined to fix Toronto's housing, homelessness crisis
articles.summary: Toronto's newly elected city council includes well-known housing rights activists and advocates supporting the homeless population. They say they're bringing their lived experiences and expertise to the council table.

articles.title: 'Bring it on,' Mississauga mayor says as real estate firms appeal city's data centre ban
articles.summary: Mississauga's new mayor says he's prepared to fight against U.S-based Prologis and Montcrest Asset Management, two companies that are challenging the city's decision to block a data centre project at the Ontario Land Tribunal.
